an1.21:1.1: The mind “developed” by way of the absorptions is “workable” ([an3.58:5.1]()), but it becomes “unworkable” due to the five hindrances ([sn46.33]()). | This chapter breaks from the pattern of the previous two, in that it is not produced from a set of five. It begins a longer series of discourses, concluding at [an1.52](), mostly marked by the term “this mind”. The use of the pronoun “this” (_idaṁ_) conveys proximity and specificity. Elsewhere it is said that “this mind” has been corrupted by greed, hate, and delusion ([sn22.100:2.5]()), or is always anxious ([sn2.17:2.1]()), or that it flounders about ([dhp34:3]()). These all refer to the mind affected by different conditions.
an1.25:1.1: Here, _pātubhūta_ (“manifested”) is a synonym for “developed”, in reference to the realization of untapped potential. [an4.162]() speaks of the degree of manifestation of the faculties.
